name: Outbreak and Disease Response — WHO and UN Practice

stations.why: The shared opener: a decontamination line run in order is the same discipline an isolation ward and a treatment centre are built on.

The first alert: a written case definition read before anything is counted, a signal verified before it is believed, a report filed at the tier the evidence supports, and a silent site chased rather than counted as zero.

The anteroom every clinical station after this one depends on: kit inspected, the donning order, a seal check every time, a buddy at the door, and the doffing order that keeps the respirator on until last.

An ordinary ward turned into an isolation area before the first patient arrives: one-way flow, suspected and confirmed kept apart, a room held at negative pressure, and hand hygiene within reach of every bed.

The daily household visit that finds the next case before it spreads: the community focal person met first, the interview held outdoors at distance, every contact found, and a sick contact referred rather than driven.

The treatment centre's gate: every arrival screened touch-free against the posted definition, suspected cases sent by their own path, and the ambulance and the family that follow handled without breaking either rule.

The camp water point the Sphere Handbook sets standards for: water treated in order, chlorine dosed from the jar test, a residual read at the tap, and latrines sited downhill with a basin at every one.
An outbreak vaccination session end to end: the cold chain proven, every vial checked, an auto-disable syringe straight into the safety box uncapped, and every person watched before they go home.

The community meeting WHO outbreak communication guidance describes: what is known and what is not, trusted voices at the front, rumours logged rather than repeated, and last week's questions answered in public.

A burial team's visit taught as one procedure for safety and dignity: the family heard first with their community representative, the body carried by the whole team, the grave marked, and a supervised doff.
The last station: a no-blame review once the outbreak is over, the frontline heard first, planned set against actual, and every lesson turned into an action with an owner and a date.

summary: Stations from the first alert to the last discharge: surveillance and case definition, PPE, an isolation ward, contact tracing, a treatment centre, water and sanitation, a vaccination line, risk communication, safe and dignified burial, and the after-action review.
union: SEIU and AFSCME public-health staff, NNU and CNA nurses, and the humanitarian workforce that deploys under UN clusters
